title: Hazel and the Bakery
premise: Sable Montrose, a marine biologist hiding from a scandal that cost him his reputation, has spent ten years writing anonymous letters to a stranger who once answered one of his own—letters signed only 'Hazel.' When Hazel finally reveals herself and moves next door to open a bakery on his small island, Sable must confront the truth: she has known who he was all along, and her arrival is no accident. As their friendship deepens into love, Sable discovers Hazel's motives are tangled with the very scandal that exiled him, forcing him to choose between protecting his invisibility and exposing the powerful man who destroyed them both. In the end, they bring the truth to light through the bakery itself—a public reckoning baked into bread and testimony—and Sable boards the last ferry not to flee, but to return with Hazel beside him.
about_author: Isandro Galloway is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's assistant who claims to have learned storytelling from fog signals and gull arguments. He writes slow-burn romances set in coastal towns where everyone knows your business except the thing that matters most.

chapters.title: Turtle Count
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. On Pelican Key, Sable counts nesting loggerheads and avoids the mainland, establishing his self-imposed exile after a research fraud scandal he didn't commit. Emotional beat: weary routine masking grief.

chapters.title: The Letters
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, flashback woven through present. We learn of ten years of letters exchanged with a stranger named Hazel—the only person who ever believed him. Beat: tenderness he doesn't let himself feel awake.

chapters.title: Moving Vans and Flour Dust
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel arrives next door, renovating the old Kestrel house into a bakery. She recognizes Sable instantly; he doesn't know she's his letter-writer. Beat: nervous hope under cheerful competence.

chapters.title: Free Samples
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Hazel engineers a first conversation over cardamom buns; Sable is prickly but thawing. She almost tells him who she is, then falters. Beat: first spark, first concealment.

chapters.title: Low Tide Confessions
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Walking the flats at low tide, Sable tells Hazel fragments of his scandal without naming names; she listens like someone who already knows. Beat: dangerous intimacy.

chapters.title: The Mayor's Welcome
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Councilman Aldous Wren, the man who framed Sable a decade ago, welcomes Hazel warmly—too warmly. Readers see she has come for him. Beat: dramatic irony tightens.

chapters.title: Oven Hours
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable starts helping at the bakery before dawn, fixing her ancient oven. Domestic closeness grows; he catches himself laughing. Beat: found family begins with the morning regulars.

chapters.title: What the Island Remembers
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Old-timer Marisol tells Hazel about the night Sable was driven out, filling gaps in her investigation. Beat: righteous anger hardening into plan.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A hurricane approaches; the island battens down. Sable and Hazel shelter together, and he nearly kisses her. Beat: suspended desire, rising dread.

chapters.title: After the Water
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Storm damage floods the hatchery; the town works side by side. Sable sees Hazel organizing everyone and realizes he loves her. Beat: community as salvation.

chapters.title: The Unsent Letter
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel drafts the letter revealing everything—her identity, Wren's crime, her decade of guilt over staying silent—and burns it instead. Beat: cowardice she despises.

chapters.title: Wren Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Wren visits the bakery, drops veiled threats about Sable's 'past,' and Sable recognizes the smell of old rot. Beat: fear resurfacing, protective instinct igniting.

chapters.title: Bread and Evidence
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel shows Sable a box: her brother was Wren's co-author who died mysteriously; her letters to Sable began as an apology she never sent. Beat: betrayal and revelation collide.

chapters.title: The Ferry Argument
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Furious that his decade of solace was surveillance-adjacent pity, Sable tells Hazel to leave on the last ferry of the season. Beat: heartbreak weaponized as self-protection.

chapters.title: Empty Ovens
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel stays anyway, reopening alone while the town watches. Sable watches from the dunes, counting turtles, unable to count her out. Beat: stubborn hope.

chapters.title: Marisol's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Marisol produces an old ledger proving Wren falsified the data Sable was blamed for. Sable must decide: stay invisible or testify. Beat: the theme made flesh—justice outside the law.

chapters.title: Midnight Bake
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sable appears at the bakery at midnight; they bake together in silence, then speak honestly—about the letters, the lies, the love neither retracted. Beat: reconciliation without absolution yet.

chapters.title: The Hearing That Isn't One
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The island holds an open meeting in the bakery; witnesses read the ledger aloud, Wren's allies defect, and the mainland press arrives uninvited. Beat: communal justice, tension peaking.

chapters.title: Wren's Last Loaf
chapters.summary: Climax. Wren attempts to burn the bakery's records; Sable and Hazel stop him, and his confession is caught on the town's phones. Beat: exposure, danger, courage.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Wren is escorted to the mainland ferry; Sable stands at the dock, invited to board and reclaim his career—and chooses to stay. Beat: inversion of exile.

chapters.title: First Rise
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Weeks later: the bakery thrives, the hatchery thrives, Sable signs his real name to a new paper. He writes her a letter by hand and delivers it in person. Beat: full-hearted beginning.

chapters.title: Hazel and the Bakery
chapters.summary: Alternating final POV. A year on, the town gathers for the bakery's anniversary; Sable proposes with a ring hidden in a proofing basket, because she'd never forgive a ruined loaf. Beat: joy earned, family chosen.
